title.zh: 卷45 志二十 时宪一 推步因革
title.en: Volume 45 Treatises 20: Calendar 1, Tui Bu Yin Ge
title.raw: 卷45 志二十 时宪一 推步因革

sentences.zh: 志二十

translations.literal: Treatise 20
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 20

sentences.zh: 時憲一

translations.literal: Shixian 1
translations.idiomatic: Shixian Calendar 1

sentences.zh: 明之大統術，本於元之授時。

translations.literal: The Ming dynasty's Datong system was based on the Yuan dynasty's Shoushi system.
translations.idiomatic: Ming astronomical reckoning in the Datong tradition stemmed from the Yuan dynasty's Shoushi calendar.

sentences.zh: 成化以後，交食往往不驗。

translations.literal: After the Chenghua reign, solar and lunar eclipses often failed to match observation.
translations.idiomatic: From the Chenghua era onward, predicted eclipses frequently did not accord with what was observed.

sentences.zh: 萬曆末，徐光啟、李之藻等譯西人之書為新法，推交食、淩犯皆密合，然未及施用。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wanli reign, Xu Guangqi, Li Zhizao, and others translated Western books into the new methods; their calculations of eclipses and planetary encroachments all matched closely, yet the methods were not put into use in time.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Wanli period, Xu Guangqi, Li Zhizao, and others translated Western works to establish the new methods; their predictions of eclipses and planetary conjunctions agreed closely with observation, but the system was never adopted before the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 世祖定鼎以後，始絀明之舊曆，依新法推算，即承用二百六十餘年之時憲術也。

translations.literal: After the Shizu Emperor established the capital, he first discarded the Ming old calendar and calculated according to the new methods—that is, the Shixian system that has been in use for more than 260 years.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Shunzhi Emperor had secured the throne, the court set aside the Ming calendar and reckoned time by the Western methods—the Shixian system that has governed Qing astronomy for more than two centuries and sixty years.

sentences.zh: 光啟等齗齗辨論，當時格而不行，乃為新朝改憲之資，豈非天意哉！

translations.literal: Guangqi and others argued vehemently, but at the time their proposals were blocked and not implemented; they thus became the material for the new dynasty's calendar reform—was this not Heaven's intent!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guangqi and his colleagues had pressed their case insistently, yet the late Ming court blocked them; their work then supplied the foundation for the Qing calendar reform—as if Heaven had reserved it for the new dynasty.

sentences.zh: 聖祖邃於曆學，定用均輪法以齊七政，以康熙甲子為元。

translations.literal: The Sage Ancestor was deeply versed in calendrical science; he fixed the use of the uniform epicycle method to align the seven luminaries, taking the jiazi year of the Kangxi reign as the epoch.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor, himself a master of astronomy, adopted the uniform epicycle method to harmonize the motions of the seven luminaries, with the jiazi year of his reign as the new epoch.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，從監臣之請，推步改橢圓法，以雍正癸卯為元。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign, at the request of the Directorate officials, astronomical calculation was changed to the elliptical method, with the guimao year of Yongzheng as the epoch.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongzheng era, on the petition of the Astronomical Directorate, computation shifted to elliptical theory, with the guimao year of Yongzheng as the new epoch.

sentences.zh: 道光中，監臣以交食分秒不合，據實測之數損益原用數，以道光甲午為元。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang reign, Directorate officials, because the minutes and seconds of eclipses did not agree, adjusted the numbers in use according to observed values, taking the jiawu year of Daoguang as the epoch.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daoguang period, when eclipse predictions disagreed with observation down to the minute, the Directorate revised the constants on the basis of actual measurements, establishing the jiawu year of Daoguang as a new epoch.

sentences.zh: 自康熙至於道光，推步之術凡三改，而道光甲午元曆僅有恒星表。

translations.literal: From Kangxi to Daoguang, the methods of astronomical calculation were changed three times, yet the Daoguang jiawu-epoch calendar had only a table of fixed stars completed.
translations.idiomatic: Between Kangxi and Daoguang the computational system was revised three times, but the Daoguang jiawu-epoch reform produced only a star table—the work on solar and lunar eclipses and the five planets remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 至於推日月交食、步五星，均未及成書雲。

translations.literal: As for calculating solar and lunar eclipses and the motions of the five planets, none reached completion in book form.
translations.idiomatic: Treatises on eclipse prediction and planetary motion, however, were never brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 西人湯若望，與徐光啟共譯新法者也，以四十二事證西人之密、中術之疏，疇人子弟翕然信之。

translations.literal: The Westerner Adam Schall, who together with Xu Guangqi translated the new methods, used forty-two points to prove the precision of Western learning and the laxity of Chinese methods; the sons and disciples of calendrical officials all believed him at once.
translations.idiomatic: Adam Schall, the Jesuit who with Xu Guangqi rendered the new astronomy into Chinese, set forth forty-two propositions demonstrating Western precision and the shortcomings of native methods; calendrical students accepted them wholesale.

sentences.zh: 宣城人梅文鼎研精天算，由授時以溯三統、四分以來諸家之術，又博考九執、回回術，而折衷於新法，皆洞其原本，究其異同，卒以績學受知聖祖，於是為推步之學者，始知中、西之學之一貫，不至眩晃於新法矣。

translations.literal: Mei Wending of Xuancheng studied celestial calculation to mastery; starting from Shoushi he traced back the methods of the Santong, Sifen, and later schools, also broadly examining the Jiuzhi and Huihui systems, and reconciling them with the new methods—he penetrated their origins and investigated their differences and similarities; he finally won recognition from the Sage Ancestor through his accumulated learning, so that scholars of astronomical calculation came to know that Chinese and Western learning were of one piece and were no longer dazzled and confused by the new methods alone.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Wending of Xuancheng mastered astronomy and mathematics, tracing from the Shoushi calendar back through the Santong, Sifen, and later traditions while also studying the Jiuzhi and Islamic systems and weighing them against the new methods. He grasped each system's foundations and compared their differences until the Kangxi Emperor took notice of his scholarship. Scholars of astronomical calculation then understood that Chinese and Western astronomy formed a single continuum, and were no longer swept away by novelty alone.

sentences.zh: 與湯若望同時入中國者為穆尼閣，傳其學於淄川薛鳳祚，而吳江人王錫闡自創新法，用以推日月食，不爽秒忽，兩家之學，皆不列於台官，然其精密，或為台臣所不及焉。

translations.literal: One who entered China at the same time as Schall was Nicolas Longobardo, who transmitted his learning to Xue Fengzuo of Zichuan; Wang Xichan of Wujiang created his own new methods, using them to calculate solar and lunar eclipses without missing by a second or an instant. The learning of both houses was not enrolled among the Observatory officials, yet in precision they sometimes surpassed the Directorate staff.
translations.idiomatic: Nicolas Longobardo arrived in China at the same time as Schall and passed his astronomy to Xue Fengzuo of Zichuan, while Wang Xichan of Wujiang devised independent methods that predicted eclipses to the exact second. Neither school held office in the Astronomical Directorate, yet their accuracy at times exceeded that of the official astronomers.

sentences.zh: 今為時憲誌，詳考其推步、七政、四餘、根理、法數著於篇，諸家論說有裨數理者，亦撮其大要載之。

translations.literal: Now this treatise on the Shixian calendar examines in detail its astronomical calculation, the seven luminaries, the four residuals, fundamental principles, and computational numbers, setting them forth in the chapters; discussions from various schools that benefit mathematical principles are also summarized and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: This treatise on the Shixian calendar sets out in detail its methods of calculation, the seven luminaries, the four residuals, underlying theory, and computational constants, while also summarizing scholarly discussions that illuminate the mathematics involved.

sentences.zh: 明大統術、回回術，康熙初用之，以詳於明史，不具論。

translations.literal: The Ming Datong system and the Huihui system were used at the beginning of Kangxi; because they are treated fully in the History of Ming, they are not discussed here in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Datong and Islamic calendars, still referenced in the early Kangxi period, are covered at length in the History of Ming and are therefore not treated here.

sentences.zh: 推步因革

translations.literal: Evolution of Astronomical Calculation
translations.idiomatic: Evolution of Astronomical Calculation

sentences.zh: 順治元年六月，湯若望言：「臣於明崇禎二年來京，曾依西洋新法釐訂舊曆，今將新法所推本年八月初一日日食，京師及各省所見食限分秒，並起復方位，圖象進呈，乞屆期遣官測驗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Shunzhi, Schall said: "Your servant came to the capital in the second year of Chongzhen of the Ming and once revised the old calendar according to Western new methods. Now I present diagrams of the solar eclipse on the first day of the eighth month of this year as calculated by the new methods—the degrees, minutes, and seconds of the eclipse limits as seen in the capital and each province, together with the positions of first contact and last contact—begging that officials be sent to test them when the day arrives."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Shunzhi 1, Schall reported: "I reached Beijing in Chongzhen 2 of the Ming and had already revised the old calendar by Western methods. I now submit charts of the solar eclipse predicted for the first day of the eighth month of this year—the magnitude in degrees, minutes, and seconds as it will appear in the capital and each province, with the bearings of first and last contact—and request that officials be dispatched to verify the prediction on the appointed day."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The order was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 七月，若望又推天象進呈。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Schall again calculated celestial phenomena and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Schall submitted further astronomical predictions.

sentences.zh: 是月禮部言：「欽天監改用新法，推注已成，請易新名，頒行天下。

translations.literal: That month the Ministry of Rites said: "The Directorate of Astronomy has changed to the new methods and completed its calculations; we request a new name and issuance throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: That month the Ministry of Rites reported: "The Astronomical Directorate has adopted the new methods and finished its ephemerides; we ask that the calendar be given a new name and promulgated empire-wide."

sentences.zh: 」睿親王言：「宜名『時憲』，以稱朝廷憲天乂民至意。

translations.literal: " The Prince Regent said: "It should be named 'Shixian' to express the court's utmost intent to model Heaven and bring order to the people."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince Regent Dorgon proposed: "Let it be called Shixian—'Season Constitution'—to reflect the court's purpose of aligning with Heaven and governing the people."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The order was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 八月丙辰朔午時，日食二分四十八秒，大學士馮銓，同若望赴觀象台測驗覆奏，惟新法一一菂合，大統、回回二曆俱差時刻，敕：「舊法歲久自差，非官生推算之誤，新法既密合天行，監局宜學習勿怠玩。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, bingchen day, at the noon hour, the solar eclipse was two parts and forty-eight seconds; Grand Secretary Feng Quan, together with Schall, went to the Observatory to test and report back: only the new methods matched in every particular; the Datong and Huihui calendars were both off in time. An edict said: "The old methods have drifted through long years—it is not the fault of the officials' calculations. Since the new methods closely match celestial motion, the Directorate should study them and not neglect or play with them."
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the eighth month, at noon, the eclipse reached two parts and forty-eight seconds of the sun's disk. Grand Secretary Feng Quan joined Schall at the Observatory to observe and report: only the new methods matched observation in every detail, while the Datong and Islamic calendars erred in timing. The throne replied: "The old systems have drifted with time—this is not the fault of the calculators. Since the new methods accord closely with the heavens, the Directorate must study them diligently and not treat them lightly."

sentences.zh: 」十月，頒順治二年時憲書。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month, the Shixian almanac for the second year of Shunzhi was issued.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Shixian almanac for Shunzhi 2 was promulgated.

sentences.zh: 若望又言：「敬授人時，全以節氣交宮與太陽出入晝刻為重。

translations.literal: Schall also said: "In reverently granting the seasons to mankind, everything depends on the solar terms' passage through the lodges and on the sun's rising, setting, and day-length."
translations.idiomatic: Schall added: "The calendar's chief duty is to regulate human time, and this rests above all on the solar terms' passage through the lodges and on the sun's times of rising, setting, and the length of day."

sentences.zh: 今節氣之日時刻分與太陽出入晝夜時刻，俱照道里遠近推算，請刊入時憲書。

translations.literal: Now the days, hours, minutes of the solar terms and the times of the sun's rising, setting, and day and night are all calculated according to distance in li; we request that these be printed in the Shixian almanac."
translations.idiomatic: The dates and times of the solar terms and the sun's rising, setting, and day-length should now be calculated for each place according to its distance from the capital; I ask that these tables be included in the Shixian almanac."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The order was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以若望掌欽天監事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Schall was put in charge of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Schall was appointed to direct the Astronomical Directorate.

sentences.zh: 若望等言：「臣等按新法推算月食時刻分秒，復定每年進呈書目，刪其復重，以免混淆。

translations.literal: Schall and others said: "We have calculated lunar eclipse times in minutes and seconds by the new methods, and have also fixed the annual list of books to be presented, deleting repetitions to avoid confusion."
translations.idiomatic: Schall and his colleagues reported: "We have computed lunar eclipse times to the second by the new methods, and have revised the annual list of works submitted to the throne, removing duplications to prevent confusion."

sentences.zh: 」二年六月，若望等言：「舊法推算本年十二月己卯朔辰時日食三分強，回回科算見食一分弱。

translations.literal: " In the sixth month of the second year, Schall and others said: "The old methods calculate a solar eclipse on the new moon of the twelfth month, jimao day, at the chen hour, of more than three parts; the Huihui section calculates a visible eclipse of a little more than one part."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Shunzhi 2 they added: "By the old methods the solar eclipse on the new moon of the twelfth month, at the chen hour, should exceed three parts of the sun's disk; the Islamic section predicts a little more than one part visible."

sentences.zh: 依新法推之，止應食半分強，且在日出之前，地平上不見，請臨期遣官測驗。

translations.literal: By the new methods it should be only a little more than half a part, and moreover before sunrise, invisible above the horizon; we request officials be sent to test when the day arrives."
translations.idiomatic: By the new methods the eclipse should amount to only a little over half a part, and it will occur before sunrise and therefore be invisible at the horizon; we again ask that officials verify this on the day."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The order was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 至期天陰雨，推驗事遂輟。

translations.literal: When the day came, the sky was overcast and rainy, and the verification was therefore abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day clouds and rain prevented observation, and the verification was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 十一月，若望以明大學士徐光啟所譯崇禎曆書改名新法曆書進呈，上命發監局官生肄習，仍宣付史館，加若望太常寺卿銜。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Schall presented the Chongzhen Calendar Book translated by the Ming Grand Secretary Xu Guangqi, renamed the New Methods Calendar Book; the emperor ordered it distributed to Directorate officials and students for study, also sent to the Historiography Office, and added Schall to the post of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Schall submitted Xu Guangqi's Chongzhen Calendar Book under the new title Calendar of the New Methods. The emperor ordered it distributed for study within the Directorate and also deposited in the Historiography Office, and promoted Schall to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 十年，賜若望通玄教師，以獎其勤勞。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was granted the title Master Who Penetrates the Mysterious, to reward his diligence.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Shunzhi he received the title Master Who Penetrates the Mysterious in recognition of his service.

sentences.zh: 若望之法，以天聰戊辰為元。

translations.literal: Schall's method takes the wuchen year of Tiancong as the epoch.
translations.idiomatic: Schall's system takes the wuchen year of the Later Jin (Tiancong) as its epoch.

sentences.zh: 分周天為三百六十度。

translations.literal: The full circuit of heaven is divided into 360 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The celestial sphere is divided into 360 degrees.

sentences.zh: 太陽一日平行五十九分八秒十九微四十九纖三十六芒，最高一年行四十五秒，戊辰年平行距冬至五十三分三十五秒三十九微，最高距冬至五度五十九分五十九秒。

translations.literal: The sun's mean daily motion is 59 minutes 8 seconds 19 microseconds 49 fine units 36 finest units; the apogee moves 45 seconds in one year; in the wuchen year mean motion from winter solstice is 53 minutes 35 seconds 39 microseconds, apogee from winter solstice is 5 degrees 59 minutes 59 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's mean daily motion is 59′8″19‴49⁗36⁘; its apogee advances 45″ per year. For the wuchen epoch year, mean motion from the winter solstice is 53′35″39‴, and the apogee lies 5°59′59″ from the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 太陰一日平行一十三度一十分三十五秒一微，自行一十三度三分五十三秒五十六微，正交行三分一十秒，月孛行六分四十一秒，戊辰年平行距冬至六宮一度五十分五十四秒四十六微，自行距冬至六宮二十五度三十二分一十五秒三十四微，正交行距冬至一宮一十四秒，月孛行距冬至十一宮六度一十九分。

translations.literal: The moon's mean daily motion is 13 degrees 10 minutes 35 seconds 1 microsecond; true motion 13 degrees 3 minutes 53 seconds 56 microseconds; node motion 3 minutes 10 seconds; lunar apogee motion 6 minutes 41 seconds; in the wuchen year mean motion from winter solstice is 6 lodges 1 degree 50 minutes 54 seconds 46 microseconds, true motion from winter solstice 6 lodges 25 degrees 32 minutes 15 seconds 34 microseconds, node from winter solstice 1 lodge 14 seconds, lunar apogee from winter solstice 11 lodges 6 degrees 19 minutes.
translations.idiomatic: The moon's mean daily motion is 13°10′35″1‴; its true (anomalistic) motion 13°3′53″56‴; its node advances 3′10″ per day; the lunar apogee advances 6′41″ per day. For the wuchen epoch, mean longitude from the winter solstice is 6 lodges 1°50′54″46‴, true longitude 6 lodges 25°32′15″34‴, the node at 1 lodge 14″, and the lunar apogee at 11 lodges 6°19′.

sentences.zh: 土星諸行應平行距冬至為十一宮十八度五十一分五十一秒，本年最高行距冬至為九宮八度五十七分五十九秒，平行距最高即引數，為二宮九度五十三分五十二秒，正交行距冬至為六宮七度九分八秒。

translations.literal: For Saturn, all motions: mean motion from winter solstice should be 11 lodges 18 degrees 51 minutes 51 seconds; this year's apogee motion from winter solstice is 9 lodges 8 degrees 57 minutes 59 seconds; mean motion from apogee, that is the equation, is 2 lodges 9 degrees 53 minutes 52 seconds; node motion from winter solstice is 6 lodges 7 degrees 9 minutes 8 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: For Saturn at the epoch: mean longitude from the winter solstice is 11 lodges 18°51′51″; the apogee for that year lies 9 lodges 8°57′59″ from the winter solstice; the equation (mean minus apogee) is 2 lodges 9°53′52″; the node stands 6 lodges 7°9′8″ from the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 一平年平行為十二度十三分三十一秒，最高行一分二十秒十二微，以最高行減平行，得十二度十二分十五秒，乃一年之引數也。

translations.literal: In a common year mean motion is 12 degrees 13 minutes 31 seconds, apogee motion 1 minute 20 seconds 12 microseconds; subtracting apogee from mean gives 12 degrees 12 minutes 15 seconds—this is the annual equation.
translations.idiomatic: In a common year Saturn's mean motion is 12°13′31″ and its apogee advances 1′20″12‴; subtracting the latter from the former yields 12°12′15″ as the annual equation.

sentences.zh: 一閏年平行為十二度十五分三十五秒，引數為十二度十四分十五秒。

translations.literal: In an intercalary year mean motion is 12 degrees 15 minutes 35 seconds, equation 12 degrees 14 minutes 15 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: In an intercalary year the mean motion is 12°15′35″ and the equation 12°14′15″.

sentences.zh: 正交行一年為四十二秒。

translations.literal: Node motion in one year is 42 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: The node advances 42″ per year.

sentences.zh: 木星諸行應平行距冬至為八宮二十八度八分三十一秒，本天最高行為十一宮二十七度十一分十五秒，平行距最高即引數，為九宮初度五十七分十六秒，正交行為六宮二十四度四十一分五十二秒。

translations.literal: For Jupiter, all motions: mean from winter solstice should be 8 lodges 28 degrees 8 minutes 31 seconds; apogee of this heaven is 11 lodges 27 degrees 11 minutes 15 seconds; mean from apogee, the equation, is 9 lodges 0 degrees 57 minutes 16 seconds; node motion is 6 lodges 24 degrees 41 minutes 52 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: For Jupiter: mean longitude from the winter solstice is 8 lodges 28°8′31″; the apogee lies at 11 lodges 27°11′15″; the equation is 9 lodges 0°57′16″; the node at 6 lodges 24°41′52″.

sentences.zh: 一平年距冬至平行為一宮零二十分三十二秒，最高行為五十七秒五十二微，兩數相減，得一宮零十九分三十四秒，乃一平年之引數也。

translations.literal: In a common year mean from winter solstice is 1 lodge 20 minutes 32 seconds, apogee motion 57 seconds 52 microseconds; subtracting the two gives 1 lodge 19 minutes 34 seconds—this is the common-year equation.
translations.idiomatic: In a common year Jupiter's mean motion from the winter solstice is 1 lodge 20′32″ and its apogee advances 57″52‴; the difference, 1 lodge 19′34″, is the annual equation for a common year.

sentences.zh: 一閏年距冬至平行為一宮零二十五分三十一秒，引數為一宮零二十四分三十三秒。

translations.literal: In an intercalary year mean from winter solstice is 1 lodge 25 minutes 31 seconds, equation 1 lodge 24 minutes 33 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: In an intercalary year the mean motion is 1 lodge 25′31″ and the equation 1 lodge 24′33″.

sentences.zh: 正交行一年為一十四秒。

translations.literal: Node motion in one year is 14 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: The node advances 14″ per year.

sentences.zh: 火星諸行應平行距冬至為五宮四度五十四分三十秒，本天最高在七宮二十九度三十分四十秒，平行距最高即引數，為九宮五度二十三分五十秒，正交行為三宮十七度二分二十九秒。

translations.literal: For Mars, all motions: mean from winter solstice should be 5 lodges 4 degrees 54 minutes 30 seconds; apogee of this heaven is at 7 lodges 29 degrees 30 minutes 40 seconds; mean from apogee, the equation, is 9 lodges 5 degrees 23 minutes 50 seconds; node motion is 3 lodges 17 degrees 2 minutes 29 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: For Mars: mean longitude from the winter solstice is 5 lodges 4°54′30″; the apogee at 7 lodges 29°30′40″; the equation 9 lodges 5°23′50″; the node at 3 lodges 17°2′29″.

sentences.zh: 一平年距冬至平行為六宮十一度十七分一十秒，最高行一分十四秒，兩數相減，得六宮十一度十五分五十五秒。

translations.literal: In a common year mean from winter solstice is 6 lodges 11 degrees 17 minutes 10 seconds, apogee motion 1 minute 14 seconds; subtracting gives 6 lodges 11 degrees 15 minutes 55 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: In a common year Mars's mean motion from the winter solstice is 6 lodges 11°17′10″ and its apogee advances 1′14″; the difference is 6 lodges 11°15′55″.

sentences.zh: 一閏年距冬至平行為六宮十一度四十八分三十六秒，引數為六宮十一度四十七分二十一秒。

translations.literal: In an intercalary year mean from winter solstice is 6 lodges 11 degrees 48 minutes 36 seconds, equation 6 lodges 11 degrees 47 minutes 21 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: In an intercalary year the mean motion is 6 lodges 11°48′36″ and the equation 6 lodges 11°47′21″.

sentences.zh: 正交行一年為五十三秒。

translations.literal: Node motion in one year is 53 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: The node advances 53″ per year.

sentences.zh: 金星諸行應平行距冬至與太陽同度，為初宮初度五十三分三十五秒三十九微，平行距最高即引數，為六宮零五十六分五十五秒，伏見行從極遠處起，為初宮九度十一分七秒，最高行在六宮零十六分六秒。

translations.literal: For Venus, all motions: mean from winter solstice should be the same degree as the sun, 1st lodge 1st degree 53 minutes 35 seconds 39 microseconds; mean from apogee, the equation, is 6 lodges 56 minutes 55 seconds; visibility motion starts from the farthest point, 1st lodge 9 degrees 11 minutes 7 seconds; apogee motion is at 6 lodges 16 minutes 6 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: For Venus: mean longitude from the winter solstice coincides with the sun at 1 lodge 0°53′35″39‴; the equation is 6 lodges 0°56′55″; visibility motion begins at greatest elongation, 1 lodge 9°11′7″; the apogee lies at 6 lodges 0°16′6″.

sentences.zh: 一平年距冬至為十一宮二十九度四十五分四十秒三十八微，自行引數為十一宮二十九度四十四分十七秒，伏見行為七宮十五度一分五十秒，最高行為一分二十一秒。

translations.literal: In a common year from winter solstice is 11 lodges 29 degrees 45 minutes 40 seconds 38 microseconds; true-motion equation 11 lodges 29 degrees 44 minutes 17 seconds; visibility motion 7 lodges 15 degrees 1 minute 50 seconds; apogee motion 1 minute 21 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: In a common year Venus's longitude from the winter solstice is 11 lodges 29°45′40″38‴; the anomalistic equation is 11 lodges 29°44′17″; visibility motion 7 lodges 15°1′50″; apogee motion 1′21″.

sentences.zh: 一閏年距冬至及自行加五十九分八秒，伏見行加三度六分二十四秒，乃一日之行也。

translations.literal: In an intercalary year from winter solstice and true motion add 59 minutes 8 seconds; visibility motion adds 3 degrees 6 minutes 24 seconds—these are one day's motions.
translations.idiomatic: In an intercalary year the daily increments are 59′8″ for mean and true longitude from the winter solstice, and 3°6′24″ for visibility motion.

sentences.zh: 金星正交在最高前十六度，即五宮十四度十六分，其行極微，故未定其率，然於最高行無大差。

translations.literal: Venus's node is 16 degrees before the apogee, that is 5 lodges 14 degrees 16 minutes; its motion is extremely slight, so its rate was not fixed, yet it makes no great difference to apogee motion.
translations.idiomatic: Venus's node lies 16° before the apogee, at 5 lodges 14°16′; its motion is so slight that no rate was assigned, though this scarcely affects apogee calculation.

sentences.zh: 水星諸行應平行距冬至與太陽同度，平行距最高即引數，為二十九度二十分二秒，伏見行從極遠處起，為三宮二十九度五十四分一十六秒，最高在十一宮零五十二分四十二秒。

translations.literal: For Mercury, all motions: mean from winter solstice should be the same as the sun; mean from apogee, the equation, is 29 degrees 20 minutes 2 seconds; visibility motion starts from the farthest point, 3 lodges 29 degrees 54 minutes 16 seconds; apogee at 11 lodges 52 minutes 42 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: For Mercury: mean longitude from the winter solstice coincides with the sun; the equation is 29°20′2″; visibility motion at greatest elongation begins at 3 lodges 29°54′16″; the apogee at 11 lodges 0°52′42″.

sentences.zh: 一平年距冬至亦與太陽同度，自行引數為十一宮二十九度四十三分五十一秒，伏見行滿三周外有一宮二十三度五十七分二十六秒。

translations.literal: In a common year from winter solstice is also the same as the sun; true-motion equation 11 lodges 29 degrees 43 minutes 51 seconds; visibility motion beyond three full circuits has 1 lodge 23 degrees 57 minutes 26 seconds.
translations.idiomatic: In a common year Mercury's longitude from the winter solstice again coincides with the sun; the anomalistic equation is 11 lodges 29°43′51″; visibility motion beyond three circuits is 1 lodge 23°57′26″.

sentences.zh: 一閏年引數為十二宮零四十二分五十九秒，伏見行全周外為一宮二十七度三分五十二秒，正交行或曰與最高同度難測，故不敢定雲。

translations.literal: In an intercalary year the equation is 12 lodges 42 minutes 59 seconds; visibility motion beyond a full circuit is 1 lodge 27 degrees 3 minutes 52 seconds; node motion—some say it is hard to measure when at the same degree as the apogee, so its rate was not dare fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In an intercalary year the equation is 12 lodges 0°42′59″ and visibility motion beyond one circuit is 1 lodge 27°3′52″. The node's motion was left undetermined, some holding that when it coincides with the apogee it cannot be measured reliably.

sentences.zh: 若望論新法大要凡四十二事：曰天地經緯，天有經緯，地亦有之，以二百五十里當天之一度，經緯皆然。

translations.literal: Schall discussed the main points of the new methods in forty-two matters: On longitude and latitude of heaven and earth—heaven has longitude and latitude, and earth also has them; 250 li correspond to one degree of heaven, for both longitude and latitude.
translations.idiomatic: Schall set forth forty-two principal points of the new astronomy. On terrestrial and celestial coordinates: as heaven has longitude and latitude, so does the earth; 250 li on earth correspond to one degree in the sky, for both coordinates alike.

sentences.zh: 曰諸曜異天，諸曜高卑相距遠甚，駁舊曆認為同心之誤。

translations.literal: On the luminaries occupying different heavens—the luminaries are vastly separated in height and depth, refuting the old calendar's error of treating them as concentric.
translations.idiomatic: On the separate spheres of the luminaries: the planets stand at very different distances from the earth, refuting the old calendars' error of placing them on concentric spheres.

sentences.zh: 曰圓心不同，太陽本圈與地不同心，二心相距，古今不等。

translations.literal: On different circle centers—the sun's primary circle and the earth are not concentric; the distance between the two centers is unequal in ancient and modern times.
translations.idiomatic: On eccentric solar motion: the sun's orbit and the earth are not concentric, and the distance between their centers varies over time.

sentences.zh: 曰蒙氣差，地有蒙氣，非先定蒙氣差不能密合。

translations.literal: On atmospheric refraction—the earth has a vaporous atmosphere; without first determining the refraction correction, close agreement cannot be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: On atmospheric refraction: the earth is wrapped in air, and predictions cannot match observation unless refraction is calculated in advance.

sentences.zh: 曰測算異古法，測天以弧三角形，算以割圜八線表。

translations.literal: On measurement and calculation differing from ancient methods—heaven is measured by spherical triangles, calculated by the eight-line table of circle division.
translations.idiomatic: On new methods of measurement and calculation: celestial observation employs spherical triangles, and computation uses the table of eight trigonometric lines derived from the circle.

sentences.zh: 曰測算皆以黃道，測天用赤道儀，所得經度不合，新法就黃道經度，通以黃赤通率表，乃與天行密合。

translations.literal: On measurement and calculation all using the ecliptic—observing heaven with the equatorial instrument, the longitudes obtained do not agree; the new methods work from ecliptic longitude and convert through the ecliptic-equatorial conversion table, and then closely match celestial motion.
translations.idiomatic: On basing all reckoning on the ecliptic: observations with the equatorial armillary yield longitudes that do not agree with theory until converted by the ecliptic-equatorial table; only then do predictions match the heavens.

sentences.zh: 曰改定諸應，從天聰二年戊辰前冬至後己卯日子正為始。

translations.literal: On revising all correspondences—starting from the zi hour of the jimao day after the winter solstice before the wuchen year of Tiancong 2.
translations.idiomatic: On revising all epoch constants: reckoning begins from the zi hour of the jimao day following the winter solstice before Tiancong 2 (wuchen).

sentences.zh: 曰求真節氣，舊法平節氣，非真節氣，今改定。

translations.literal: On seeking true solar terms—the old methods used mean solar terms, not true solar terms; this is now revised.
translations.idiomatic: On true solar terms: the old system used mean terms rather than true terms; this has now been corrected.

sentences.zh: 曰盈縮真限，用授時消分為平歲，更以最高最卑差加減之，為定歲。

translations.literal: On true limits of expansion and contraction—using Shoushi's reduction minutes as the mean year, then adding and subtracting the apogee and perigee difference to obtain the true year.
translations.idiomatic: On true solar inequality: the mean tropical year follows the Shoushi reduction method, then apogee and perigee corrections yield the true year.

sentences.zh: 曰表測二分，舊法以圭表測冬至，非法之善者，今用春秋二分，較二至為密。

translations.literal: On gnomon measurement of the equinoxes—the old method measured winter solstice with the gnomon, not the best of methods; now the spring and autumn equinoxes are used, which is more precise than comparing the two solstices.
translations.idiomatic: On gnomon measurement at the equinoxes: measuring only the winter solstice, as the old method did, is inferior; using both equinoxes yields greater precision than relying on the solstices alone.

sentences.zh: 曰太陽出入及晨昏限，從京師起算，各處有加減。

translations.literal: On the sun's rising and setting and morning-evening limits—calculated from the capital, with additions and subtractions for each place.
translations.idiomatic: On times of sunrise, sunset, and twilight: tables are computed from Beijing, with corrections for each locality.

sentences.zh: 曰晝夜不等，其差較一刻有奇，一緣黃道夏遲冬疾，一緣黃赤二道廣狹不同距，則率度不同分。

translations.literal: On day and night being unequal—the difference is rather more than one quarter-hour; one reason is the ecliptic's summer slowness and winter swiftness, another is the different widths and distances of the ecliptic and equator, so the rate per degree differs in minutes.
translations.idiomatic: On unequal day and night: the difference amounts to somewhat more than one quarter-hour, partly because the sun moves more slowly in summer and faster in winter along the ecliptic, and partly because the ecliptic and equator differ in width and separation, altering the minutes per degree.

sentences.zh: 曰改定時刻，定晝夜為九十六刻。

translations.literal: On revising the time divisions—fixing day and night at 96 quarters.
translations.idiomatic: On revising the time system: day and night are each divided into 96 quarters (ke).

sentences.zh: 曰置閏不同，舊法用平節氣置閏，非也，改用太陽所躔天度以定節氣。

translations.literal: On intercalation being different—the old method used mean solar terms to place intercalary months, which is wrong; now the degrees of heaven traversed by the sun are used to fix the solar terms.
translations.idiomatic: On intercalation: the old practice of inserting leap months by mean solar terms was incorrect; intercalation now follows the sun's actual longitude.

sentences.zh: 曰太陰加減，朔望止一加減，餘日另有二三，均數多寡不等。

translations.literal: On lunar additions and subtractions—at new and full moon there is only one correction; on other days there are two or three more, with mean numbers of unequal quantity.
translations.idiomatic: On lunar corrections: at new and full moon only one equation applies, but on other days two or three additional corrections are needed, each of varying magnitude.

sentences.zh: 曰月行高卑遲疾，月行轉周之最高極遲，最卑極疾，五星準此。

translations.literal: On the moon's motion being slow at apogee and swift at perigee—at the highest point of its revolving circuit it is extremely slow, at the lowest extremely swift; the five planets follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: On lunar anomaly: the moon moves slowest at apogee and fastest at perigee; the five planets obey the same principle.

sentences.zh: 曰朔後月見遲疾，一因自行度遲疾，一因黃道升降斜正，一因白道在緯南緯北。

translations.literal: On the moon's visibility after new moon being early or late—one cause is the slowness or swiftness of true motion, one is the ecliptic's rising, falling, obliquity, and directness, one is whether the white path is south or north of the latitude.
translations.idiomatic: On the timing of first visibility after new moon: it depends on the moon's anomalistic motion, on the obliquity and inclination of the ecliptic, and on whether the lunar path lies north or south of the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 曰交行加減，月在交上，以平求之必不合，因設一加減為交行均數。

translations.literal: On node-motion corrections—when the moon is at the node, seeking by mean motion will certainly not agree; therefore one correction is set as the mean number for node motion.
translations.idiomatic: On node-motion corrections: when the moon is at a node, mean-motion calculation will not suffice, so an equation for node motion is introduced.

sentences.zh: 曰月緯距度，舊法黃白二道相距五度，不知朔望外尚有損益，其至大之距，五度三分之一。

translations.literal: On the moon's latitude distance—the old method held the ecliptic and white paths five degrees apart, not knowing that beyond new and full moon there are further additions and subtractions; the greatest distance is five and one-third degrees.
translations.idiomatic: On lunar latitude: the old system fixed the separation of the ecliptic and lunar path at five degrees, unaware that latitude varies beyond new and full moon; the maximum separation is five and one-third degrees.

sentences.zh: 曰交食有無，月食以距黃道緯度較月與地景兩半徑並，日食則以距度較日月兩半徑並，距度為小則食，大則不食。

translations.literal: On whether eclipses occur—for lunar eclipses compare latitude distance from the ecliptic with the combined semidiameters of moon and earth-shadow; for solar eclipses compare distance with the combined semidiameters of sun and moon—if distance is smaller there is an eclipse, if larger there is none.
translations.idiomatic: On whether an eclipse occurs: for a lunar eclipse, compare the moon's latitude with the sum of the semidiameters of the moon and earth's shadow; for a solar eclipse, compare the separation of sun and moon with the sum of their semidiameters. If the separation is less, an eclipse occurs; if greater, it does not.

sentences.zh: 曰日月食限不同，月食則太陰與地景兩周相切，以其兩視半徑較白道距黃道度，又以距度推交周度定食限，日食必加入視差而後得距度。

translations.literal: On solar and lunar eclipse limits being different—for lunar eclipses the moon's circle and the earth-shadow circle are tangent; compare their two apparent semidiameters with the white path's latitude from the ecliptic, and also use distance to derive nodal circuit degrees to fix the eclipse limit; for solar eclipses parallax must be added before distance is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: On differing eclipse limits: a lunar eclipse requires the moon's orbit and the earth's shadow to be tangent; compare their apparent semidiameters with the moon's latitude and derive the nodal arc to determine the limit. For solar eclipses, parallax must be included before the separation can be found.

sentences.zh: 曰日月食分異同，距度在月食為太陰心實距地景之心，在日食為日月兩心之距，但日食不據實距而據視距。

translations.literal: On solar and lunar eclipse magnitudes differing and agreeing—for lunar eclipses distance is the true distance from the moon's center to the earth-shadow's center; for solar eclipses it is the distance between the two centers, but solar eclipses use not true distance but apparent distance.
translations.idiomatic: On eclipse magnitude: for lunar eclipses the relevant separation is the true distance between the centers of the moon and earth's shadow; for solar eclipses it is the apparent separation of the sun and moon, not their true distance.

sentences.zh: 曰實食中食，以地心之直線上至黃道者為主，日月五星兩居此線之上，則實食也；

translations.literal: On true eclipse and central eclipse—taking the straight line from the earth's center up to the ecliptic as the standard, when sun, moon, and five stars both lie on this line, there is a true eclipse;
translations.idiomatic: On true and central eclipse: when sun, moon, or planets all lie on the line from the earth's center to the ecliptic, a true eclipse occurs;

sentences.zh: 月與五星各居本輪之周，地心直線上至黃道，而兩本輪之心俱當線上，則中食也。

translations.literal: the moon and five stars each occupy their own circles; the line from the earth's center up to the ecliptic, and both primary circle centers lie on the line—then there is a central eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: a central eclipse occurs when the line from the earth's center meets the ecliptic and both orbital centers lie upon it.

sentences.zh: 曰視食，日食有天上之實食，有人所見之視食，視食依人目與地面為準。

translations.literal: On apparent eclipse—solar eclipses have a true eclipse in the heavens and an apparent eclipse as seen by people; apparent eclipse takes the human eye and the ground surface as its standard.
translations.idiomatic: On apparent eclipse: every solar eclipse has both a true (geocentric) phase and an apparent phase as seen from the earth, the latter reckoned from the observer's eye and the local horizon.

sentences.zh: 曰黃道九十度為東西差之中限，論天頂則高卑差為正下，南北差為斜下，而東西差獨中限之一線為正下，以外皆斜下。

translations.literal: On the ecliptic's ninety degrees as the central limit of east-west difference—speaking of the zenith, altitude difference is straight below, north-south difference is obliquely below, while east-west difference alone has the central limit's one line as straight below, all outside being obliquely below.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninety-degree point of the ecliptic as the central limit for east-west parallax: at the zenith, altitude correction is vertical and north-south correction oblique; only along the central meridian is east-west correction vertical, elsewhere it is oblique.

sentences.zh: 論其道則南北差為股，東西差恒為勾，高卑差恒為弦。

translations.literal: Speaking of their paths, north-south difference is the leg, east-west difference is always the other leg, altitude difference is always the hypotenuse.
translations.idiomatic: In geometric terms, north-south parallax is the base, east-west parallax the perpendicular, and altitude parallax the hypotenuse.

sentences.zh: 至中限則股弦為一線，無勾矣。

translations.literal: At the central limit base and hypotenuse become one line, and there is no perpendicular.
translations.idiomatic: At the central limit the base and hypotenuse coincide, and the perpendicular vanishes.

sentences.zh: 曰三視差，以地半徑為一邊，以太陽太陰各距地之遠為一邊，以二曜高度為一邊，成三角形，用以得高卑差，又偏南而變緯度得南北差；

translations.literal: On the three parallaxes—taking earth's semidiameter as one side, the sun's and moon's respective distances from earth as one side, the two luminaries' altitude as one side, forming a triangle, used to obtain altitude difference; also by deviation south changing latitude to obtain north-south difference;
translations.idiomatic: On the three parallaxes: form a triangle with the earth's radius, the body's distance from earth, and its altitude to obtain altitude parallax; derive north-south parallax from its declination;

sentences.zh: 以黃道九十度限偏左偏右而變緯度，得東西差。

translations.literal: by the ecliptic's ninety-degree limit deviating left or right and changing latitude, obtain east-west difference.
translations.idiomatic: and east-west parallax from its position east or west of the ecliptic's central meridian.

sentences.zh: 曰外三差，東西、南北、高卑之差，皆生於地徑，外三差不生於地徑而生於氣。

translations.literal: On the outer three differences—east-west, north-south, and altitude differences all arise from earth's diameter; the outer three differences do not arise from earth's diameter but from the atmosphere.
translations.idiomatic: On the outer three corrections: east-west, north-south, and altitude parallax all depend on the earth's size; three further corrections arise not from the earth's diameter but from the atmosphere.

sentences.zh: 一，清蒙氣差；

translations.literal: First, clear atmospheric refraction difference;
translations.idiomatic: First, refraction in clear air;

sentences.zh: 二，清蒙徑差；

translations.literal: second, clear atmospheric semidiameter difference;
translations.idiomatic: second, apparent enlargement of the disk through the atmosphere;

sentences.zh: 三，本輪徑差。

translations.literal: third, primary-circle semidiameter difference.
translations.idiomatic: third, correction for the orbital radius.

sentences.zh: 曰虧復不一，非二時折半之說，新法以視行推變時刻，則了然於虧復時刻不一之故。

translations.literal: On first and last contact not being equal—it is not the theory of halving two times; the new methods use apparent motion to derive changing times, making clear why first and last contact times are unequal.
translations.idiomatic: On unequal times of first and last contact: the old notion of dividing the eclipse duration in half is wrong; computing by apparent motion shows why these times differ.

sentences.zh: 曰交食異算，諸方各以地徑推算交食時刻及日食分。

translations.literal: On eclipses calculated differently—each region calculates eclipse times and solar eclipse magnitude from its own earth-diameter.
translations.idiomatic: On local eclipse calculation: each place computes eclipse times and magnitude according to its own longitude and latitude.

sentences.zh: 曰日食變差，據法應食而實不見食，必此日此地之南北差變為東西差，此千百年偶遇一二次，非無有者。

translations.literal: On solar eclipse variation—when by the method there should be an eclipse but none is actually seen, necessarily on that day at that place north-south difference has changed into east-west difference; this occurs once or twice in a thousand years by chance, not that it never happens.
translations.idiomatic: On anomalous solar eclipses: when theory predicts an eclipse but none is seen, north-south parallax must have shifted into east-west parallax at that place and time—an event that may occur once or twice in a millennium.

sentences.zh: 曰推前驗後，新法諸表，上溯下沿，開卷了然，不費功力。

translations.literal: On projecting forward and verifying backward—the new methods' tables, tracing up and extending down, are clear at a glance when the book is opened, without wasted effort.
translations.idiomatic: On forward projection and backward verification: the new tables permit instant lookup in either direction without laborious calculation.

sentences.zh: 曰五星準日，舊法於合伏日數，時多時寡，徒以段目定之，不免有差，今改正。

translations.literal: On the five planets following the sun—in the old method the days of conjunction and visibility were sometimes many, sometimes few, fixed only by section headings, inevitably with error; this is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On planetary motion modeled on the sun: the old method's day-counts for conjunction and visibility varied inconsistently because they relied on tabular sections alone; this has been corrected.

sentences.zh: 曰伏見密合，舊法五星伏見惟用黃道距度，非也，今改正。

translations.literal: On conjunction and visibility matching closely—the old method used only ecliptic distance for the five planets' visibility and hiding, which is wrong; this is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On precise prediction of planetary visibility: the old method relied only on ecliptic longitude, which was inadequate; this too has been corrected.

sentences.zh: 曰五星緯度，太陰本道斜交黃道，因生距度與陰、陽二曆，五星亦然，新法一一詳求，舊未能也。

translations.literal: On the five planets' latitude—the moon's primary path obliquely crosses the ecliptic, giving rise to distance and the yin and yang calendars; the five planets are likewise; the new methods seek each in detail, which the old could not.
translations.idiomatic: On planetary latitude: the moon's orbit crosses the ecliptic obliquely, producing latitude and the yin-yang lunar tables; the five planets follow the same principle, which the new methods calculate in full detail—something the old system could not achieve.

sentences.zh: 曰金水伏見，金星或合太陽而不伏，水星離太陽而不見，用渾儀一測便知，非舊法所能。

translations.literal: On visibility of metal and water planets—Venus sometimes conjoins the sun without hiding, Mercury departs from the sun and is not seen; one measurement with the armillary sphere reveals this, beyond what old methods could do.
translations.idiomatic: On the visibility of Venus and Mercury: Venus may conjoin the sun without disappearing from view, and Mercury may stand apart from the sun yet remain invisible—a fact revealed at once by the armillary sphere, beyond the reach of older methods.

sentences.zh: 曰五星測法，測五星須用恒星為準。

translations.literal: On methods of measuring the five planets—measuring the five planets must use fixed stars as standard.
translations.idiomatic: On measuring the five planets: fixed stars must serve as the reference points.

sentences.zh: 曰恒星東移，恒星以黃道極為極，各宿距星時近赤極，亦或時遠赤極，由黃赤二道各極不同，非距星有異行或易位。

translations.literal: On fixed stars shifting east—the fixed stars take the ecliptic pole as pole; each lodge's determinant star is sometimes near the equatorial pole, sometimes far from it, because the ecliptic and equator each have different poles—not because determinant stars have different motion or change position.
translations.idiomatic: On the eastward drift of fixed stars: they are measured from the ecliptic pole, so each lodge's determinant star appears sometimes nearer and sometimes farther from the equatorial pole, because the ecliptic and equatorial poles differ—not because the stars themselves change course or position.

sentences.zh: 曰定恒星大小有六等之別，前此未聞。

translations.literal: On fixing fixed stars' magnitudes into six grades of distinction—this had not been heard of before.
translations.idiomatic: On stellar magnitudes ranked in six grades—a classification unknown before.

sentences.zh: 曰天漢釋疑，新法測以遠鏡，天漢乃無算小星攢聚而成。

translations.literal: On resolving doubts about the River of Heaven—measured by the new methods with the telescope, the River of Heaven is formed by countless small stars clustered together.
translations.idiomatic: On the Milky Way: observation through the telescope shows it to be an aggregation of innumerable faint stars.

sentences.zh: 曰四餘刪改，羅睺即白道之正交，計都即中交，月孛乃月行極高之點。

translations.literal: On revising the four residuals—Rahu is the white path's ascending node, Ketu the descending node, Yuebo the moon's highest point of motion.
translations.idiomatic: On revising the four residuals: Rahu is the ascending node of the lunar path, Ketu the descending node, and Yuebo the moon's apogee.

sentences.zh: 至紫[A12L]一餘，無數可定，明史附會，今俱改刪。

translations.literal: As for the one residual Ziqi, no numbers can fix it; the History of Ming forced a connection—all are now revised and deleted.
translations.idiomatic: As for the residual Ziqi, no parameters can be determined; the Ming History forced a connection with it—all such entries have now been removed.

sentences.zh: 曰測器，新法增置者，曰象限儀、百遊儀、地平儀、弩儀、天環天球紀限儀、渾蓋簡平儀、黃赤全儀，而新製之遠鏡，尤為測星要器。

translations.literal: On measuring instruments—those added by the new methods are: the quadrant instrument, the hundred-motion instrument, the horizon instrument, the crossbow instrument, the celestial ring and celestial globe limit-recording instrument, the simplified armillary-sphere instrument, the full ecliptic-equatorial instrument; and the newly made telescope is especially the essential instrument for measuring stars.
translations.idiomatic: On instruments: the new methods added the quadrant, the universal instrument, the horizon circle, the cross-staff, the celestial ring and globe, the simplified armillary sphere, and the full ecliptic-equatorial sphere; above all, the newly made telescope became indispensable for stellar observation.

sentences.zh: 曰日晷，為地平晷、三晷、百遊晷、通光晷。

translations.literal: On sundials—there are the horizon dial, the triple dial, the hundred-motion dial, and the light-passing dial.
translations.idiomatic: On sundials: the horizon dial, triple dial, universal dial, and light-passing dial.

sentences.zh: 此外更有星晷、月晷，以備夜測之用。

translations.literal: Beyond these there are also star dials and moon dials, to prepare for night observation.
translations.idiomatic: Star and moon dials were also added for nighttime observation.

sentences.zh: 若望所言，大抵據新法以詆舊術之疏，然新法之精蘊，亦盡於此矣。

translations.literal: What Schall said mostly relied on the new methods to denounce the laxity of old techniques, yet the essential profundity of the new methods is also fully contained in this.
translations.idiomatic: Schall's exposition chiefly used the new methods to expose the shortcomings of older systems, yet the essential substance of the new astronomy is fully summarized here.

sentences.zh: 十四年四月，前回回科秋官正吳明炫言：「臣祖默河亦裏等十八姓，本西域人，自隋開皇己未抱其學重譯來朝，授為日官。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourteenth year, the former Huihui Section Director of Autumn Offices Wu Mingxuan said: "Your servant's ancestor Mohe Yili and the other eighteen surnames were originally people of the Western Regions; from the jiwei year of Sui Kaihuang they brought their learning, retranslated, and came to court, appointed as sun officials."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Shunzhi 14, Wu Mingxuan, former director of the Islamic astronomical section, reported: "My ancestor Mohe Yili and seventeen other clans came from the Western Regions. In Kaihuang jiwei of the Sui they brought their learning to court and were appointed calendrical officials."

sentences.zh: 一千五十九年，專司星宿行度吉凶，每年推算太陰五星淩犯，天象占驗，日月交食，即以臣科白本進呈為定例。

translations.literal: For 1,059 years they have exclusively managed the auspice and inauspice of star-lodge motions, annually calculating lunar and five-planet encroachments, celestial phenomena for verification, and solar and lunar eclipses, presenting memorials from our section's white copies as fixed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: For 1,059 years our section has calculated the motions of the luminaries, planetary conjunctions, celestial omens, and eclipses, submitting annual reports as established precedent.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，本監掌印湯若望令臣科凡日月交食及太陰五星淩犯、天象占驗俱不必奏進。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, the Directorate seal-holder Schall ordered our section that all solar and lunar eclipses, lunar and five-planet encroachments, and celestial verification need not be memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3, Schall as director ordered that our section need no longer submit reports on eclipses, planetary conjunctions, or celestial omens.

sentences.zh: 臣查若望所推七政，水星二、八月皆伏不見，今水星二月二十九日仍見東方，又八月二十四日夕見，關係象占，不敢不據實上聞。

translations.literal: Your servant has checked Schall's calculations of the seven luminaries: Mercury in the second and eighth months should both be hidden and invisible; now Mercury on the twenty-ninth day of the second month is still seen in the east, and again on the evening of the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month—this concerns omen interpretation, and I dare not fail to report truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: I find that by Schall's calculations Mercury should be invisible in the second and eighth months, yet on the twenty-ninth day of the second month it was still visible in the east, and on the evening of the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month it appeared again—matters bearing on celestial omens that I must report faithfully.

sentences.zh: 乞復立回回科，以存絕學。

translations.literal: I beg that the Huihui Section be re-established to preserve this dying learning."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the Islamic section be restored to preserve this endangered tradition."

sentences.zh: 」奏下所司。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 時新安衛官生楊光先叩閽進摘謬論，糾湯若望新法之謬，且言：「時憲書有『依西洋新法』五字尤不合。

translations.literal: At this time Yang Guangxian, an official student of Xin'an Guard, knocked at the gate and presented Extracted Errors, impeaching the errors of Schall's new methods, and also saying: "The Shixian almanac's five characters 'according to Western new methods' are especially improper."
translations.idiomatic: At this time Yang Guangxian, a student of the Directorate from Xin'an, presented his Extracted Errors impeaching Schall's new methods, and objected that the phrase "according to Western new methods" on the Shixian almanac was especially improper.

sentences.zh: 」又進選擇議，糾若望選榮親王葬期用洪範五行，山向、日月俱犯忌殺。

translations.literal: " He also presented Selection Discourse, impeaching Schall's selection of the burial date for Prince Rong using the Hongfan Five Phases—the mountain direction and sun and moon all violated taboo killings.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a Selection Discourse charging that Schall, in choosing the burial date for Prince Rong by the Hongfan Five Phases, had violated taboos in mountain orientation, sun, and moon.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年十二月，禮部議「時憲書麵『依西洋新法』五字擬改『奏準』二字」，從之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Kangxi, the Ministry of Rites deliberated: "The five characters 'according to Western new methods' on the face of the Shixian almanac are proposed to be changed to the two characters 'memorial approved'"—the order was followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Kangxi 3 the Ministry of Rites proposed replacing the five characters "according to Western new methods" on the almanac cover with the two characters "memorial approved," and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 四年，議政王等言：每日百刻，新法改為九十六刻；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Prince Regents and others said: daily hundred quarters—the new methods changed this to ninety-six quarters;
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 4 the Prince Regents reported: the old division of the day into one hundred quarters was changed to ninety-six by the new methods;

sentences.zh: 二十八宿次序，湯若望將觜、參二宿改易前後；

translations.literal: the order of the twenty-eight lodges—Schall changed the sequence of the Zi and Shen lodges;
translations.idiomatic: the order of the twenty-eight lodges was altered when Schall reversed the positions of Zi and Shen;

sentences.zh: 又將四餘刪去紫炁，俱不合。

translations.literal: also the four residuals had Ziqi deleted—all improper.
translations.idiomatic: and Ziqi was removed from the four residuals—all improper changes.

sentences.zh: 其選擇不用正五行，用洪範五行，以致山向、日月俱犯忌殺，事犯重大，將湯若望及科官等分別擬淩遲斬決。

translations.literal: In his selections he did not use the orthodox Five Phases but the Hongfan Five Phases, causing mountain direction and sun and moon all to violate taboo killings—a matter of grave offense; Schall and the section officials were separately proposed for death by slicing and decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: He had used the Hongfan Five Phases rather than the orthodox system in selecting the burial date, violating taboos in mountain orientation, sun, and moon—a grave offense for which Schall and the section officials were sentenced to execution.

sentences.zh: 敕湯若望從寬免死，時憲科李祖白等五人俱處斬。

translations.literal: An edict granted Schall leniency and spared his life; five men of the Shixian Section including Li Zubai were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Schall was spared by imperial grace, but five Shixian-section officials including Li Zubai were executed.

sentences.zh: 於是復用大統舊術，以楊光先掌監務，光先抗疏屢辭，不允。

translations.literal: Thereupon the old Datong methods were restored, with Yang Guangxian in charge of Directorate affairs; Guangxian submitted remonstrances repeatedly declining, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The old Datong system was restored and Yang Guangxian placed in charge of the Directorate; he repeatedly submitted memorials declining the post, but was not permitted to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 光先於推步之學本不深，唐熙七年，謂明年當閏十二月，尋知其誤，自行檢舉，而時憲書已頒行，乃諭天下停止閏月雲。

translations.literal: Guangxian's learning in astronomical calculation was not deep to begin with; in the seventh year of Tangxi he said the next year should have an intercalary twelfth month; soon knowing his error, he reported himself—but the Shixian almanac had already been issued, so an edict told the realm to stop the intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxian was never deeply versed in astronomical calculation. In Kangxi 7 he declared that the following year required an intercalary twelfth month, then discovered his error and reported it himself—but the almanac had already been issued, and the throne ordered the intercalary month cancelled throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 是年監副吳明烜言：「古法差謬，五官正暨回回科所進各不同，立加校正。

translations.literal: That year Deputy Director Wu Mingxuan said: "The ancient methods are erroneous; what the Directors of the Five Offices and the Huihui Section submit each differs—correction should be applied at once."
translations.idiomatic: That year Deputy Director Wu Mingxuan reported: "The restored methods are in error, and the calculations submitted by the Five Offices and the Islamic section disagree; corrections must be made immediately."

sentences.zh: 」下禮部議。

translations.literal: " It was sent down to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 禮部覆奏：「五官正戈繼文等所算七政金水二星差錯太甚，主簿陳聿新所推七政未經測驗，亦有差錯，監副吳明烜所推七政與天象相近，理應頒行，仍令監臣同四科官，每日晝測晷景以定節氣，夜測月五星以定行度。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites replied: "The seven luminaries calculated by Director Ge Jiwen and others have gross errors for metal and water; Registrar Chen Yuxin's calculations of the seven luminaries have not been tested and also have errors; Deputy Director Wu Mingxuan's seven luminaries are close to celestial phenomena and should be issued; still order Directorate officials together with the four sections' officers to measure gnomon shadows by day to fix solar terms and observe moon and five planets by night to fix motions."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry replied: "Director Ge Jiwen's calculations of Venus and Mercury are grossly in error; Registrar Chen Yuxin's figures have not been verified and are also wrong; Deputy Director Wu Mingxuan's results accord with observation and should be adopted. Directorate officials and the four sections should measure gnomon shadows by day to fix the solar terms and observe the moon and planets by night to determine their motions."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The order was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 十一月，西人南懷仁言所頒各法不合天象，乃召南懷仁、利類思、安文思及監官馬祐、楊光先、吳明烜等至東華門，大學士李霨傳諭：「授時乃國家要政，爾等勿挾宿仇，以己為是，以彼為非。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Westerner Ferdinand Verbiest said the methods issued all failed to match celestial phenomena; Verbiest, Ferdinand de Tournon, and Gabriel de Magalhaes, together with Directorate officials Ma You, Yang Guangxian, Wu Mingxuan, and others were summoned to the Donghua Gate; Grand Secretary Li Ji transmitted the instruction: "Granting the seasons is a vital state affair—you must not harbor old grudges, taking yourselves as right and others as wrong."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Verbiest reported that the issued methods did not match the heavens. Verbiest, de Tournon, de Magalhaes, and Directorate officials including Ma You, Yang Guangxian, and Wu Mingxuan were summoned to the Donghua Gate, where Grand Secretary Li Ji conveyed the emperor's words: "Calendar reform is a vital state affair; do not let old grudges lead you to insist you alone are right."

sentences.zh: 是者當遵用，非者當更改，務期歸於至善。

translations.literal: What is right should be followed; what is wrong should be changed, striving to reach the utmost good."
translations.idiomatic: What is correct should be adopted; what is wrong should be revised, until the system reaches perfection."

sentences.zh: 」十二月，南懷仁劾吳明烜所造康熙八年七政時憲書糾謬，下王大臣、九卿、科道會議，議政王等言：「乞派大臣同南懷仁等測驗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Verbiest impeached errors in the Kangxi 8 seven-luminaries Shixian almanac made by Wu Mingxuan; it was sent down to princes, ministers, the Nine Chief Ministers, and the censorate for joint deliberation; the Prince Regents said: "We beg that great ministers be dispatched together with Verbiest and others to test."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Verbiest impeached errors in Wu Mingxuan's Shixian almanac for Kangxi 8. The case was referred to princes, ministers, the Nine Chief Ministers, and the censorate; the Prince Regents proposed that senior officials test the rival methods alongside Verbiest.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣圖海、李霨等二十人赴觀象台測驗。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Tu Hai, Li Ji, and twenty others were sent to the Observatory to test.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai, Li Ji, and twenty others were dispatched to the Observatory to conduct the tests.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，議政王等議覆：「圖海等赴觀象台測驗，南懷仁所言皆合，吳明烜所言皆謬，問監正馬祐等，亦言南懷仁所算實與天象合。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year, the Prince Regents reported: "Tu Hai and others went to the Observatory to test; everything Verbiest said matched, everything Wu Mingxuan said was wrong; asking Director Ma You and others, they also said Verbiest's calculations truly matched celestial phenomena."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Kangxi 8 the Prince Regents reported: "At the Observatory, Verbiest's predictions matched observation in every case and Wu Mingxuan's in none; Director Ma You and his colleagues confirmed that Verbiest's calculations accorded with the heavens."

sentences.zh: 竊思百刻雖行之已久，但南懷仁九十六刻之法既合天象，自應頒用。

translations.literal: We reflect that the hundred quarters, though long in use, yet since Verbiest's ninety-six-quarter method matches celestial phenomena, it should naturally be issued.
translations.idiomatic: Although the hundred-quarter day had long been in use, Verbiest's ninety-six-quarter system matched the heavens and should be adopted.

sentences.zh: 又南懷仁言羅睺、計都、月孛係推算所用，故載於七政之後，其紫炁星無用處，不應造入。

translations.literal: Also Verbiest said Rahu, Ketu, and Yuebo are used in calculation, therefore recorded after the seven luminaries; the Ziqi star has no use and should not be fabricated into the system.
translations.idiomatic: Verbiest also explained that Rahu, Ketu, and Yuebo are computational points listed after the seven luminaries, whereas the star Ziqi serves no purpose and should be omitted.

sentences.zh: 應自康熙九年為始，用九十六刻之曆」，時明烜言「臣祗知天文，不知曆法」，光先言「臣不知曆法，惟知曆理」。

translations.literal: From the beginning of Kangxi 9, the ninety-six-quarter calendar should be used"; at this Mingxuan said "Your servant knows only astronomy, not calendrical methods"; Guangxian said "Your servant does not know calendrical methods, only calendrical principles."
translations.idiomatic: The ninety-six-quarter calendar was to take effect from Kangxi 9. Mingxuan said, "I know astronomy but not calendar-making"; Guangxian said, "I know calendrical principle but not calendar-making."

sentences.zh: 光先語尤不遜，褫職。

translations.literal: Guangxian's words were especially impertinent; his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxian's language was especially disrespectful, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 三月，授南懷仁欽天監監副。

translations.literal: In the third month, Verbiest was appointed Deputy Director of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Verbiest was appointed deputy director of the Astronomical Directorate.

sentences.zh: 先是監官依古法推算，康熙八年十二月應置閏，南懷仁言雨水為正月中氣，是月二十九日值雨水，即為康熙九年正月，不應置閏，置閏當在明年二月。

translations.literal: Previously Directorate officials calculated by ancient methods; the twelfth month of Kangxi 8 should have an intercalation; Verbiest said rain-water is the mid-term of the first month—on the twenty-ninth day of that month rain-water falls, so it is the first month of Kangxi 9 and should not be intercalated; intercalation should be in the second month of next year.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate officials using the old methods had placed an intercalary month in the twelfth month of Kangxi 8. Verbiest argued that rain-water, the mid-term of the first month, fell on the twenty-ninth day of that month, making it already the first month of Kangxi 9; intercalation belonged in the second month of the following year.

sentences.zh: 監官多直懷仁，從其言，改閏九年二月，於是大統、回回兩法俱廢，專用西洋法，如順治之初。

translations.literal: Most Directorate officials sided with Verbiest; following his words, intercalation was moved to the second month of the ninth year; thus both Datong and Huihui methods were abandoned, using only Western methods as at the beginning of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Most officials supported Verbiest, intercalation was set for the second month of Kangxi 9, and both the Datong and Islamic systems were abandoned in favor of Western methods, as in early Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 八月，南懷仁劾楊光先誣陷湯若望叛逆，議政王等議「湯若望應復通微教師，照原品賜恤，楊光先應反坐」。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Verbiest impeached Yang Guangxian for falsely charging Schall with treason; the Prince Regents deliberated: "Schall should be restored as Master Who Penetrates the Mysterious, with original rank and posthumous grant; Yang Guangxian should receive counter-charge."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Verbiest impeached Yang Guangxian for falsely accusing Schall of treason. The Prince Regents proposed restoring Schall's title and honors and imposing counter-penalties on Yang Guangxian.

sentences.zh: 敕「免議」。

translations.literal: An edict said "exempt from deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the matter dropped.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月，新造儀象誌告成，南懷仁加太常寺卿銜。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year, the new Instruments and Observations was completed; Verbiest was added to the post of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Kangxi 13 the new Instruments and Observations was completed, and Verbiest received the additional title of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 十四年二月，諭監副安泰從何君錫學古曆法。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourteenth year, an edict ordered Deputy Director An Tai to learn ancient calendrical methods from He Junxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Kangxi 14 the emperor ordered Deputy Director An Tai to study the ancient calendar under He Junxi.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月，欽天監奏五月朔日食，監副安泰依古法算，應食五分六十秒，南懷仁新法隻應食二十微三分秒之一。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year, the Directorate memorialized a solar eclipse on the new moon of the fifth month; Deputy Director An Tai by ancient methods calculated it should be five parts and sixty seconds; Verbiest's new method showed only twenty microseconds and one-third of a second.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Kangxi 15 the Directorate reported a solar eclipse on the new moon of the fifth month. By ancient methods An Tai predicted 5 parts 60 seconds; Verbiest's new method predicted only 20 microseconds and one-third of a second.

sentences.zh: 至期登台測驗，酉正食甚，將及一分，戌初刻復圓，古法所推分數失之甚遠，而新法亦不甚合。

translations.literal: When the day came they mounted the terrace to test; at you-zheng the eclipse was greatest, reaching nearly one part; at the beginning of the xu quarter it ended—the ancient method's magnitude was far off, and the new method also not very close.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the eclipse they observed from the terrace: greatest eclipse at you-zheng, nearly one part of the sun's disk, ending at the start of the xu quarter. The ancient prediction was far wrong, and the new method also fell somewhat short.

sentences.zh: 南懷仁曰：「此清蒙氣之所為，蒙氣能映小為大故也。

translations.literal: Verbiest said: "This is caused by clear atmospheric refraction—refraction can make the small appear large."
translations.idiomatic: Verbiest explained: "Clear atmospheric refraction magnifies small objects—that is why the eclipse appeared larger than calculated."

sentences.zh: 十七年七月，欽天監進呈康熙永年表三十二卷。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventeenth year, the Directorate presented the Kangxi Perpetual Tables in thirty-two volumes.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kangxi 17 the Directorate submitted the Kangxi Perpetual Tables in thirty-two volumes.

sentences.zh: 二十二年十月，監臣推算盛京九十度表告成。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-second year, Directorate officials' calculation of the ninety-degree table for Mukden was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kangxi 22 the ninety-degree table for Mukden was completed.

sentences.zh: 初，南懷仁奏：「各省北極高度不同，其交合之時刻食分俱不等，全憑各省之九十度表推算。

translations.literal: Initially Verbiest memorialized: "Each province has a different north polar altitude; the times of conjunction and eclipse magnitude are all unequal, entirely depending on each province's ninety-degree table for calculation."
translations.idiomatic: Verbiest had earlier reported: "Each province's north polar altitude differs, so eclipse times and magnitudes differ and must be calculated from local ninety-degree tables."

sentences.zh: 向來不知盛京北極高度，即用京師之九十度表，今測得盛京北極比京師高二度，請依其高度推算九十度表。

translations.literal: Formerly the north polar altitude of Mukden was unknown and the capital's ninety-degree table was used; now measurement shows Mukden's north pole is two degrees higher than the capital—please calculate a ninety-degree table according to its altitude."
translations.idiomatic: Previously Mukden's latitude was unknown and the capital's table was used; measurement now shows Mukden's north pole is two degrees higher than Beijing's—please compute a table for that latitude."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The order was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 至是，以盛京九十度表進呈，諭「永遠遵守」雲。

translations.literal: At this time the Mukden ninety-degree table was presented; an edict said "observe forever."
translations.idiomatic: The Mukden table was then submitted with orders to observe it permanently.

sentences.zh: 四十一年十月，大學士李光地以宣城貢生梅文鼎曆學疑問三卷進呈，上曰：「朕留心曆算多年，此事朕能決其是非。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the forty-first year, Grand Secretary Li Guangdi presented three volumes of Calendrical Questions by Mei Wending of Xuancheng; the emperor said: "I have attended to calendrical calculation for many years; I can decide right and wrong in this matter."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kangxi 41 Grand Secretary Li Guangdi presented Mei Wending's three-volume Calendrical Questions; the emperor said, "I have studied astronomy for many years and can judge these matters myself."

sentences.zh: 」乃親加批點還之，事具梅文鼎傳。

translations.literal: " He personally added marginal notes and returned it—the matter is recorded in Mei Wending's biography.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated the work in his own hand and returned it, as recorded in Mei's biography.

sentences.zh: 文鼎論中、西二法之同異曰：「今之用新曆也，乃兼用其長，以補舊法之未備，非盡廢古法而從新法術也。

translations.literal: Wending discussed the similarities and differences of Chinese and Western methods, saying: "Today's use of the new calendar is to employ both strengths together, supplementing what the old methods lack—not utterly abandoning ancient methods to follow new techniques."
translations.idiomatic: Mei wrote on the relation of Chinese and Western astronomy: "The new calendar today draws on both traditions to supplement what the old methods lacked—it does not simply discard native methods for Western ones."

sentences.zh: 夫西曆之同乎中法者，不止一端。

translations.literal: Where Western astronomy agrees with Chinese methods, there is more than one point.
translations.idiomatic: Western astronomy agrees with Chinese methods in more than one respect.

sentences.zh: 其言五星之最高加減也，即中法之盈縮曆也，在太陰，則遲疾曆也。

translations.literal: Its discussion of the five planets' apogee additions and subtractions is the Chinese method's expansion-contraction calendar; for the moon, it is the slow-swift calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Its treatment of planetary apogee correction corresponds to the Chinese expansion-contraction tables; for the moon, to the slow-swift tables.

sentences.zh: 其言五星之歲輪也，即中法之段目也。

translations.literal: Its discussion of the five planets' annual circles is the Chinese method's section headings.
translations.idiomatic: Its annual circles for the five planets correspond to the Chinese section tables.

sentences.zh: 其言恒星東行也，即中法之歲差也。

translations.literal: Its discussion of fixed stars shifting east is the Chinese method's precession.
translations.idiomatic: Its eastward drift of fixed stars is the Chinese precession.

sentences.zh: 其言節氣之以日躔過宮也，即中法之定氣也。

translations.literal: Its discussion of solar terms by the sun's passage through lodges is the Chinese method's true qi.
translations.idiomatic: Its solar terms defined by the sun's lodge passage are the Chinese true solar terms.

sentences.zh: 其言各省真節氣不同也，即中法之裏差也。

translations.literal: Its discussion of different true solar terms in each province is the Chinese method's li difference.
translations.idiomatic: Its provincial variation in true solar terms is the Chinese li difference.

sentences.zh: 但中法言盈縮遲疾，而西說以最高最卑明其故；

translations.literal: But Chinese methods speak of expansion, contraction, slow, and swift, while Western theory explains the cause through apogee and perigee;
translations.idiomatic: Chinese methods record expansion, contraction, slow, and swift motion; Western theory explains these by apogee and perigee;

sentences.zh: 中法言段目，而西說以歲輪明其故；

translations.literal: Chinese methods speak of section headings, while Western theory explains the cause through annual circles;
translations.idiomatic: Chinese methods use section tables; Western theory explains them through annual circles;

sentences.zh: 中法言歲差，而西說以恒星東行明其故。

translations.literal: Chinese methods speak of precession, while Western theory explains the cause through fixed stars' eastward motion.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese methods record precession; Western theory explains it through the stars' eastward drift.

sentences.zh: 是則中曆所言者當然之運，而西曆所推者其所以然之理，此其可取者也。

translations.literal: Thus what Chinese astronomy states is the course things naturally take, while Western astronomy deduces the underlying reasons—this is where it is valuable.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese astronomy describes what happens; Western astronomy explains why—therein lies its value.

sentences.zh: 若夫定氣裏差，中曆原有其法，但不以法曆耳，非古無而今始有也。

translations.literal: As for true qi and li difference, Chinese astronomy originally had the methods, but did not put them in the calendar—it is not that antiquity lacked them and only now they exist.
translations.idiomatic: True solar terms and li difference were already known in Chinese astronomy but not always applied in official calendars—not inventions of the West.

sentences.zh: 西曆始有者，則五星之緯度是也。

translations.literal: What Western astronomy first had is the latitude of the five planets.
translations.idiomatic: What Western astronomy first supplied is planetary latitude.

sentences.zh: 中曆之緯度，惟太陽、太陰有之，而五星則未有及之者。

translations.literal: Chinese astronomy's latitude applies only to sun and moon; the five planets had not yet been treated.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese methods calculated latitude only for the sun and moon, not yet for the five planets.

sentences.zh: 今西曆之五星有交點、有緯行，亦如太陽太陰之詳明，是則中曆缺陷之大端，得西法以補其未備矣。

translations.literal: Now Western astronomy's five planets have nodes and latitude motion, as detailed as for sun and moon—this is the greatest gap in Chinese astronomy, filled by Western methods.
translations.idiomatic: Western methods now give the five planets nodes and latitude as fully as for the sun and moon, filling the greatest gap in Chinese astronomy.

sentences.zh: 夫於中法之同，亦既有以明其所以然之故，而於中法之未備者，又有以補其缺，於是吾之積候者，得彼說而益信，而彼說之若難信者，亦因吾之積候而有以知其不誣，雖聖人復起，亦在所兼收而並取矣。

translations.literal: In what agrees with Chinese methods, the reasons can be made clear; in what Chinese methods lacked, Western methods can supply the deficiency; thus our accumulated observations gain credibility from Western theory, and what seemed hard to credit in Western theory is confirmed by our observations—not false. Even if a sage arose again, he would gather both together.
translations.idiomatic: Where the traditions agree, Western theory clarifies the reasons; where Chinese methods were incomplete, Western methods supply the lack. Long observation confirms Western theory, and Western claims once doubted are vindicated by Chinese records. A sage would embrace both.

sentences.zh: 五十年十月，上諭大學士等：「天文曆法，朕素留心，西法大端不誤，但分刻度數之間，積久不能無差。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fiftieth year, the emperor instructed the grand secretaries: "Astronomical calendrical methods—I have always attended to them; the main points of Western methods are not wrong, but between minute divisions accumulated years cannot be without error."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kangxi 50 the emperor told the grand secretaries: "I have long studied astronomy; Western methods are sound in principle, but minute errors accumulate over time."

sentences.zh: 今年夏至，欽天監奏午正三刻，朕細測日景，是午初三刻九分。

translations.literal: This year's summer solstice—the Directorate memorialized wu-zheng three quarters; I finely measured the sun's shadow—it was wu-initial three quarters nine minutes."
